title: Rewiring the paralyzed body's false alarm.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran scripts/paper_context.py: Europe PMC reports isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, hasDbCrossReferences=N, hasTMAccessionNumbers=N; no PMCID so no full text and no supplementary file listing; zero accessions, zero NCBI links, zero Zenodo/Dryad hits. Fetched the PubMed record (PMID 42531402) directly: Science vol 393, issue 6810, pages 470-471, a single author (Jan Elaine Soriano, NeuroRestore/EPFL), one-sentence abstract. Two web searches confirmed it is a commentary on a separate research article.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The scientific content (that hyperactive Vsx2-expressing excitatory spinal neurons underlie autonomic dysreflexia, a dangerous blood-pressure surge after spinal cord injury, and that repeated epidural electrical stimulation reverses it in mice, rats and humans) comes from the abstract and from search summaries of the commented-on paper, not from any file I opened. I could not read the Perspective's own text at all because it is paywalled.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset. This is a two-page Science Perspective/commentary (pp. 470-471, one author) about someone else's research article; it reports no new measurements and has no data availability statement, no supplementary files, and no accessions. Verified via Europe PMC flags (hasData=N, hasSuppl=N, no PMCID) and the PubMed record, not just the abstract.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessed: no data of any kind, so there is no column and no label.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not assessed: no files. Row count is null because none was ever seen.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessed: no files to compare against the text.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the item is a commentary with no underlying data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use spinal stimulation settings and body signals to predict blood-pressure surges in people with spinal cord injury.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on time-series recordings of blood pressure and heart rate paired with epidural electrical stimulation settings from spinal-cord-injured animals and patients. Number of examples: unknown, because this commentary contains no data.
plain_idea.predict: Whether and how severely an autonomic dysreflexia episode (a sudden, dangerous rise in blood pressure triggered by ordinary sensory input) occurs. The true answer would come from direct arterial or cuff blood-pressure measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians managing spinal cord injury would gain an early-warning or closed-loop controller for a complication that can cause stroke, and rehabilitation engineers could tune stimulation automatically. But none of that is possible from this paper, which contributes no measurements.

ml_idea: None available from this item. The underlying research article it comments on (Nature, 'A neuronal architecture underlying autonomic dysreflexia', doi 10.1038/s41586-025-09487-w, PMC12571909) does contain single-cell transcriptomics and physiology and is open access; if a candidate in this area is wanted, that paper, not this commentary, is the one to evaluate.

effort.compute_note: No estimates possible: there is no data to load, so nothing to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check the publication type and page count first. Two pages (470-471), one author, a one-sentence abstract and Europe PMC's hasData=N flag identify a Perspective in under a minute, which is the whole evaluation.

verdict_reason: A1 fails outright: this is a paywalled two-page Science Perspective commenting on another group's Nature paper. It reports no new measurements, has no supplementary files, no accessions and no data availability statement (confirmed by Europe PMC flags and the PubMed record, not just the abstract). There is nothing to download, so no project can be built on it. The research article it discusses is a legitimate separate candidate.
